newsitem.title: USA: LOOP offshore operations seen back up Saturday.
newsitem.headline: LOOP offshore operations seen back up Saturday.

text.p: The Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP), the only deepwater port in U.S. waters, should have offshore operations back to normal on Saturday after Hurricane Danny passed through the area earlier Friday, a LOOP official said.

"The offshore terminal is still evacuated. We are assessing the situation to see if we can get people back on by this evening. I anticipate we'll be operating by sometime tomorrow," said Tom McCauley, vice president of operations for LOOP.
He said that onshore operations continued to operate normally and there were no delays to deliveries.
One ship was due to have offloaded crude oil on Friday and that will be delayed until offshore operations are back to normal.

Meanwhile, the center of Danny, which was upgraded to a Hurricane as it hit land in Louisiana on Friday morning, was located near latitude 29.6 north longitude 89.5 west or about 45 miles southeast of New Orleans at 0700 Central Daylight Time (CDT), The National Weather Service in Miami reported.
